title: Impasto
look: Oil paint laid on thick: ridged brush strokes in warm colour on a canvas weave.

doc.essence: A small oil sketch painted wet into wet: every area is a crowd of short, loaded strokes with a light ridge on each, over a canvas you can still feel.
doc.notIt: Not watercolor (opaque, thick, warm, no paper showing), not crayon (strokes are wide and ridged, not waxy scribbles), not clay (texture is the brush, not the thumb).
doc.shapes: A dark umber contour painted with a loaded brush that wobbles a little. Inside, short curved strokes in three values of the area's colour.
doc.colour: Every colour warmed towards ochre and pushed a touch more saturated. Eyes and line in burnt umber.
doc.eyes: Solid umber, like a last dab of dark paint.
doc.motion: Smooth, with a faint boil so the painted edge never sits perfectly still.
pitfalls: Stroke patterns behind the eyes compete with the face: keep the stroke values close to the base colour.
Very dark palettes lose the ridges: the highlight stroke must stay visible.
